transferred: Inventory first-party source before applying narrower eligibility rules.
Keep parser and report semantics family-local while sharing the complete/partial/unsupported/failed vocabulary.
Prove copied on-demand closures, native go test, final artifacts, and source immutability per skill.
Treat generated, testdata, fixture, vendor, dependency, and build-constrained source as explicit policy cases.
Batch syntax files through one Go compiler-driver launch when a repository scan needs per-file AST facts.
did_not_transfer: TypeScript lexical walkers and Compiler API loaders.
One universal AST or cross-skill Go fact schema.
One common failure policy: audit is atomic, standard coverage may be partial, and omnibus refuses ambiguous build selection.
One common output lifecycle: explanation artifacts are target-keyed while most detectors write isolated reports.
review_findings_that_became_contracts: Implicit GOOS/GOARCH filename constraints are not comment-only build tags.
Only the final filename suffix constrains a Go file; names such as clean_linux_impl.go are ordinary.
The canonical generated marker may follow long leading line or block comments before package.
Narrow targets and symlinks cannot bypass project-root-relative exclusions.
Failed reruns cannot leave a prior complete explanation, annotations, sidecars, or latest pointer visible.
Artifact cleanup must reject source-file, source-directory, and symlinked report-directory overlap.
Generic and parenthesized direct Go calls remain visible to syntax standards.

tooling_decision.current: Keep analyzers and launchers in each selected skill closure.
tooling_decision.candidate: A generated/tested Go source-policy template for tool preflight, generated/build classification, and project-relative exclusions.
tooling_decision.promotion_trigger: Adopt only if it reduces total code while the installer can carry an explicit self-contained closure for every consumer; do not introduce a hidden repository import.
not_now: go/packages or go/types before semantic-project skills demonstrate the need

next_cohort_guidance: Complete find-duplication as a separate detector decision before semantic work.
Pilot no more than three semantic/project skills before considering shared go list, go/packages, or go/types facts.
Use one locked module with generated, testdata, vendor, build-tag, implicit filename, malformed, and missing-tool cases from the start.
Measure repeated Go process launches before extracting or batching another runtime helper.
